items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: Benny told me he was playing with a piano player, Duke Pearson, over at the Vanguard

ctx.x: Yes. And Benny Powell come by my house one night and he said, 'I know you haven't had your horn out of the case.' He said, 'Let me play your horn.' So a friend of mine, Dickie [Cohen], was playing the piano. So I went on and instead of handing the horn to Benny Powell, I went

on and played the tune. And Benny's mouth dropped open, my wife, Jackie, shed a few tears, you know. And I went on and played the horn like that. So Benny told me he was playing with a piano player, Duke Pearson, over at the Vanguard, so Benny told me, he said, "Look," he said, "I'm going to have a record date." He said, "You go over there and take your horn and just sit there and hold it. You don't have to play," you know, "if you don't want to or don't feel like it." He knew very well I wasn't going to sit…
So I went on and I played, did the best I could. So finally Benny had me do it, you know, a couple of times for him again, a couple of spots. And I called Tony Bennett, talked to Tony.
